**Individuation** — what makes something one thing, and the same thing over time or across descriptions — individuation, numerical identity and diversity, individuality and persistence of things of any kind, biological individuality and organisational closure. Selves are self and persons are personhood (group: philosophy; ADR-015, ADR-024).

[CLAIM-264](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-264.md)'s exact half shows that agreement on a restricted probe family does not fix identity; this claim draws the rule for reading such agreement as evidence. It is an argument, not a theorem, so it is interpretive. It does not say which probes to choose, or that held-out probes are neutral. | Active |
| [CLAIM-328](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-328.md) v3 | When the continuities that ordinarily come bundled in a collective (legal franchise, civic role, interpersonal transmission, narrative and place) are separated, several later collectives can each be a genuine successor of the earlier one in a different respect, without any of them, or the earlier collective, having branched in numerical identity | A4's H5 of the exchange of 2026-10-16, in its weak form, on the Washington Senators. The league's successor to the original club is the Twins; the city's is the expansion Senators; the city's present team claims its history through place and narrative. Promoted from a section of [QUESTION-118](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-118.md) at the owner's word. It concerns plural successor relations, not branching identity, and rests on one documented case with no data on how supporters divided. | Active |
| [CLAIM-329](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-329.md) v5 | A collective that replaces all its members persists, when it does, by causal transmission of the organization that produces it, not by resemblance: an organization of the same kind that arises independently is not its continuation, and a lapse in its coherence need not end it | A5, A8 and A9 of the exchange of 2026-10-16. A9 §9 separated three persistences that dissociate: state persistence (a variable changes slowly), dynamical persistence (characteristic responses continue) and historical persistence (the producing processes are transmitted and reconstituted across successive populations). A5: "a system's ability to reproduce itself as the same kind is not automatically sufficient for its numerical persistence as the same individual." The second time the record meets "causal-organizational continuity": [CLAIM-280](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-280.md) noted A10 §4.3's of 2026-10-13 and did not file it. It does not say what must be transmitted, or settle branching successors. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-331](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-331.md) v9 | A level of organization has a temporal facet as well as a compositional one: higher-level variables are characteristically slower and longer-lived than the activity that produces them, though slowness is a mark of a level and not its definition | The owner's, U8 of the exchange of 2026-10-16: "'higher level' doesn't just mean in terms of abstractions over abstractions, we should also expect 'higher level' effects to be on slower timescales than 'lower level' effects." A8 took it and qualified it: a market can crash and a stadium can chant in seconds, so timescale is "a facet of organizational level, not ... an ordering that must hold in every case". Simon's near-decomposability already ties weak coupling between blocks to slow aggregate dynamics ([LIT-905](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-905.md)). The claim does not say that a slow variable is thereby a level, a system or an individual. | Active |
| [CLAIM-360](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-360.md) | The deep-versus-shallow learning results separate three effects that aggregate loss conflates: a larger realizable function class, a larger set reachable within a fixed data and compute budget, and a different internal organization with the same attainable outcomes; the deep linear results show the third, the random-hierarchy results the second, and the depth-separation result for products of inputs the first, at fixed size | The owner's, U38 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, on A37's proposed experiment: "I think we may already have an empirical demonstration that would be useful here in the wide vs deep literature." A38 refined it into three effects, (A) enlarged realizable function class, (B) enlarged budgeted reachable set, (C) new internal organization without better attainable outcomes, filed Saxe et al. under C and the random hierarchy model under B, and said A "needs a separately established expressivity restriction". The record has one: Rolnick and Tegmark ([THEORY-206](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-206.md)), a separation at fixed neuron count. The sharp edge: which effect a result shows depends on the budget, and A38 warned against "depth produces individuation while width merely provides redundant capacity". | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-361](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-361.md) | Relief of an organization's frustration must be judged for an identified organization against a fixed reference set of its original demands, under an explicit correspondence between earlier and later demands: a demand excised or suppressed has changed the comparison and has not been satisfied, an endogenous revision of what the organization maintains is a transformation of it and not relief, and learning can change which processes bear the demands | The owner's prompt, U38 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, on A37's line that deleting a demand "has changed the comparison problem": "it might be helpful to connect back to our notions of individuation". Worked out by A38 and restated by A39 §2B and A43. Relief, as enlargement of the compatibility complex ([CLAIM-347](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-347.md)), is judged over a fixed reference set of demands, for an organization identified before and after, under a stated correspondence. Watson's comparison ([THEORY-232](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-232.md)) is already relative to a decomposition; what this adds is the comparison across time, when the decomposition itself changes. The sharp edge: it does not say transformation is worse than relief, only that it answers a different question. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-367](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-367.md) v4 | Whether a training-time regulatory condition belongs to a network depends on which unit is individuated for the training dynamics and whose jurisdiction governs the updates; in conventional training most of that governance falls to the optimizer–model–data system, so a condition of training is not thereby a condition of the network | The owner's correction, U31 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: "it might help clarify things if we apply our individuation and volition frameworks to this system", the system being a deep network during training (U30). A31 granted it: "applying individuation first, then volition, then affect exposes a problem in our previous discussion". Individuated for the training dynamics, the unit is at least the network–optimizer pair; mapped through the six relations of will-organization, most of the governance of updates is outside the network's jurisdiction. So optimization difficulty in conventional training is real and belongs to the training system. The sharp edge: it does not say the governance is unreal, or that a network cannot come to hold some of it. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-388](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-388.md) v3 | Exact dynamical closure of a collective variable does not require a nearly decomposable block: in a linear Gaussian VAR(1) with uniform coupling among n units, the sum of all units is exactly dynamically independent at every stable coupling strength, while every partition of the units into two or more groups couples as strongly across its edges as within them | From A5 of the exchange of 2026-10-19 on coarse-to-fine processes, which gave the two-unit continuous-time case (ż = (b − a)z for z = x₁ + x₂) and the boxed slogan "Exact aggregation ⇏ near-decomposability". Made exact here for n units with [THEORY-733](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-733.md)'s sufficiency condition, and checked numerically. It answers the converse half of [QUESTION-221](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-221.md). It does not say the closed sum is one system ([QUESTION-218](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-218.md)), and it is about partitions of the units: in the eigenbasis of A the same system is exactly decomposable, which is the point. | Active |
| [CLAIM-405](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-405.md) v2 | An individuation is well defined only once its criterion is fixed (the target it serves, the transformations its unity must survive, the scale), and that dependence does not make it arbitrary: once the criterion is fixed a verdict can be false, and differently fixed criteria can pick out units of one system whose boundaries cross rather than nest, none of them less real for it | The individuation counterpart of the owner's normative thesis [CLAIM-363](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-363.md) ("once they are fixed, the judgment can be false"), as A8 and A9 of the exchange of 2026-10-20 put it, on the owner's U8 question about "contextuality/relativity/subjectivity". A8 §9: "the underlying system is objectively real, while some scientifically meaningful properties of its descriptions are objectively relational." A9: "an individuation claim can be objectively assessed once its relevant organizational criteria are specified", and "A system may exhibit several objectively grounded forms of unity that need not share the same boundary." [CLAIM-152](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-152.md) gives the relativity; this claim adds that relativity is not arbitrariness. It bears on QUESTION-065 without answering it. It does not say which criterion is right. | Active |
| [CLAIM-414](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-414.md) v4 | Matched ordinary trajectories can conceal differences in an interpretation's efficacy, in the allocation of that efficacy, and in the maintenance of its enabling constraints: in two finite constructions, systems that agree under ordinary operation differ in each, and a specified intervention exposes the difference that passive observation of the matched trajectories does not | A10 of the exchange on experience and interpretation, re-run here. Three one-bit systems behave alike when the interpretation is 0. Under an intervention that sets it to 1, the first never acts on it, the second acts at once, and the third acts one step late, because its own interpretation opens the gate. Two two-constraint systems have the same trajectory, (1,1) throughout. A single perturbation runs one into (0,0) and leaves the other restored to (1,1): one maintains its constraints by [CLAIM-395](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-395.md)'s minimal slow–fast closure, the other is reset from outside. These are [CLAIM-407](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-407.md)'s lesson about governance and [CLAIM-194](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-194.md)'s about boundaries, applied to interpretation. | Active |
| [CLAIM-417](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-417.md) v4 | What the record explained by "self" in its dispositional, persisting, self-governing and integrated senses is better explained by organizational perspectives, with a perspective, its carriers, its lineage and its representations kept apart; the subject sense stays a separate question, and narrative, presented and modeled selves involve representations that may describe a perspective, attribute it to a bearer or construct an owner, none of them the perspective itself | The owner's, at U31 of the exchange of 2026-10-22: the record's earlier "selves" are "better described as 'organizational perspectives'". A31 agreed with a narrowing that this claim keeps. Selfhood "was carrying several explanatory burdens that we can now separate", and the subject sense is "A separate question". The sharp edge is what the replacement must keep apart: a perspective as realized, in one carrier or distributed across several, a recognizable character shared by many, a causal lineage of realizations, and representations of any of these. The exchange ran these together; the claim does not. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-418](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-418.md) v2 | Possessing, enacting or being shaped by an organizational perspective does not establish an independent agent, and perspectival, agential and institutional boundaries need not coincide: several agents can share a perspective, one agent can act through several, and a perspective can be reproduced with no agent governing it; where a perspective contributes to an agent's activity it can enable and constrain the exercise of agency, and that exercise can reproduce or transform it, while whether agency universally requires such a perspective stays open | From the branch of the exchange of 2026-10-22: the owner's question at U38, "what's the relationship between perspective and agency?", A38's answer, and A39's request that it be recorded. A38: "Perspective concerns how a situation becomes meaningful and actionable. Agency concerns how an organized system can make a difference to what happens." The claim takes the half A38 called "substantially safer": not every organization of practical significance is an agent. It leaves A38's other half, that every rich exercise of agency involves such an organization, as open. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-420](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-420.md) v2 | A historical figure's influence can persist in three separable ways, as a story about them, as a perspective transmitted from them, and as later organizations that descend from their activity, and causal descent is not perspectival inheritance: a movement founded to oppose someone descends from them without continuing their perspective | From the owner's U38 of the exchange of 2026-10-22, corrected. The owner contrasted "immortality" through positive influence that reinforces itself across generations with notoriety whose influence is "self-undermining", the figure's story persisting while their perspective does not. A38 corrected the example and declined the tidy mapping of positive to self-reinforcing and notorious to self-undermining. What survives is the distinction: "The persistence of a story about someone is not equivalent to the persistence of that person's perspective." | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-421](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-421.md) v3 | The cessation of an organizational perspective's enactment need not imply the loss of the dispositions, capacities or reproductive relationships from which it can be reinstated: an interruption can be of activation (the disposition is held but not engaged or retrievable), of enactment (held, but the material, institutional or social conditions for exercising it are gone) or of reproduction (held by some bearers, but the processes that pass it on are damaged), and temporary unavailability is not extinction, though prolonged interruption of reproduction can end a tradition | From the branch of the exchange of 2026-10-22, at the owner's U37: the doorway effect as perspective meeting grounded experience, and the perspectival interruptions of the Chinese Cultural Revolution. A37 drew the distinction the record's account of perspective lacked, between the conditions under which a perspective is acquired or reproduced and the conditions under which it stays available. The edge: a doorway and a political revolution are not the same kind of forgetting, and the claim says only that both separate a capacity's existence from the availability of the conditions for exercising it. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-424](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-424.md) v2 | Reflexive governance of an organization's perspectival arrangements, making the conditions that govern its own interpretation, evaluation and action available for effective examination and revision, is a capacity some organizations of perspective have and others lack, not what makes something a perspective or a self; and the capacity to revise those standards is not the capacity to revise them well | A37's definition, from the exchange of 2026-10-22, re-scoping [CLAIM-284](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-284.md). [CLAIM-284](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-284.md) says that a self, in the self-governing sense, is an organization that governs the conditions of its own persistence. Every reply from A31 on read it as "a proposed special case": a perspective can be reproduced, persist and adapt without governing its own reproduction. The edge is A37's: "the capacity to revise the standards of evaluation is not equivalent to the capacity to revise them well", which keeps [CLAIM-288](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-288.md)'s objection standing. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-454](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-454.md) | A latent feature or mode recovered from an organization's members' activity is at most a constituent of an organizational perspective, not the perspective: a feature allocation says which members take part in which modes, and whether those modes are organized into one perspective depends on the relations of access, uptake and authority among their carriers, which the same allocation leaves open | From the Northstar turns of the exchange "Experimental Infrastructure Review", where the owner proposed inferring an organization's perspectives with hLDA (T21) and the Indian buffet process (T22). Every reply made the same reservation, and T22 put it most plainly: "None of those ingredients alone is the perspective. The organized relationship among them is." It is the criterion [QUESTION-276](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-276.md)'s answer has to meet. It does not say features are useless, or that no perspective is ever one feature's carriers. It says the allocation underdetermines the perspective. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-463](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-463.md) | Restoring the conditions under which a capacity was lost need not restore the capacity: where the activity that maintains it reinforces itself, the same conditions can sustain both the capacity and its absence, so a capacity lost past a threshold returns only under conditions better than those it was lost under, or by rebuilding the activity directly, and restoring it can cost more than preserving it would have | A4's claim candidate from the exchange "About the Chagossians" of 2026-10-26, "Resource restoration does not imply organizational restoration", which the first filing declined because [CASE-111](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-111.md) already derives it; the owner asked for it to be filed as a claim with its connection to the case. Demonstrated by [CASE-111](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-111.md)'s normal form: in the bistable range, returning the parameter to its pre-collapse value leaves maintenance at zero. The edge: a possibility shown in a model, not a finding about any grant program, people or institute, and a slow recovery is not evidence of the threshold. | Active |
| [CLAIM-473](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-473.md) | Coupling locally described systems necessarily induces a separation of time scales between their collective behaviour and their relative behaviour | The owner's, the second half of U20 of the exchange of 2026-10-27: "coupling inertial frames necessarily induces scale separation (way less confident about this one than the former assertion)". Filed as said, with "inertial frames" read as the local descriptions of [CLAIM-471](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-471.md). Rejected on filing: the necessity is refuted by conservatively coupled oscillators ([CLAIM-481](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-481.md)), which A20, A21 and A23 all gave. The owner's doubt was well placed; what survives is a condition, and the condition is the interesting part. | Rejected |
| [CLAIM-474](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-474.md) v2 | From interconnection to individuation, five relationships are distinct achievements and none implies the next: interconnection fixes what joint behaviour is possible, compatibility which local descriptions admit a coherent whole, dynamics which compatible, frustrated or differentiated organizations persist, individuation which persistent organizations have sufficiently robust identity and boundaries, organizational autonomy being the further question which of those also help maintain their own constitutive constraints, and inquiry which of them can measure and revise their own models and apparatuses under resource bounds; the research program is to find the conditions for each transition | Filed at the owner's review of the pull request, which asked for a synthesis "From Interconnection to Individuation: A Relational Constraint Research Program" that would make the theory "legible as a research program with distinct testable transitions, rather than a cluster of philosophically suggestive analogies". It references the record's claims rather than restating them. Its content is the list of places where one achievement does not yield the next, each with a source the record has read. The central experiment, in which physical coupling, correspondence maps and apparatus revision are manipulated independently, is [CASE-179](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-179.md). The open questions it organizes are [QUESTION-282](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-282.md), [QUESTION-283](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-283.md), [QUESTION-285](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-285.md), [QUESTION-281](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-281.md) and [QUESTION-115](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-115.md). | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-477](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-477.md) v2 | Relata stand to relations as realizations stand to specifications: what an entity is, is partly fixed by the constraints on the configurations of entities and relations it can enter, and those constraints are themselves realized and maintained by something, so neither relata nor relations, nor specifications nor realizations, are prior without qualification | The owner's, U8 of the exchange of 2026-10-27, "maybe relata:relations::realization:specifications/constraints?", after U6 had set the record's ambitions as "extremely abstract and unrestricted". A8 sharpened it: "Relata are to relational structure somewhat as realizations are to specifications—but relations themselves also have realizations", and added the recursion, that constraints "are themselves realizations within larger relational structures". Filed unrestricted in domain, as the frame of which [CLAIM-151](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-151.md) and [CLAIM-136](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-136.md) are domain cases. It is not a structural realism that eliminates relata, and satisfying a specification is not being produced by it. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-478](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-478.md) | Scale separation helps make structure and not only marks it: where some degrees of freedom settle fast relative to others, the relation they settle into is a constraint on the system over the window between the two time scales, so what is a realization at one scale works as a constraint at another; and organization can make new separations in turn, as when modes slow near an instability and become order parameters, so time-scale hierarchies and constraints can produce one another | The owner's, U12 of the exchange of 2026-10-27: "I think we may still have a coverage gap wrt scale separation and how that participates in creating structure". A12 agreed and found that the gap was synthesis, not literature: the record held [CLAIM-331](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-331.md), [CLAIM-327](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-327.md), [THEORY-661](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-661.md), [CLAIM-395](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-395.md) and Mori–Zwanzig readings. It goes beyond [CLAIM-331](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-331.md), on which slowness is a mark of a level, in two ways: separation makes constraints, and constraints can make separation. It supplies the mechanism for [CLAIM-477](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-477.md)'s recursion. It does not say that slowness is sufficient or necessary for a constraint, or that a constraint is an individual. | Proposed |
